issues: The diff changes one hyperparameter, DEPTH from 8 to 6. It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines or the evaluation call. The harness also reported no integrity flags.

The change cannot invalidate the result. In a fixed 300 s budget a smaller model gets more optimizer steps, so a better val_bpb is plausible. The model dimension probably scales with depth, so the model also gets narrower. That is a legitimate capacity trade-off.

I can't recompute z exactly because the incumbent's standard deviation isn't given. The candidate mean is 1.08335, which is 0.03115 below the incumbent mean of 1.1145. A z of 7.593 implies a standard error of about 0.0041. That is consistent with the two candidate runs being tightly clustered (1.0835 and 1.0832) and 16 incumbent runs. The direction and size of the reported z match the numbers.
Minor point: the candidate rests on only 2 runs. Their spread (0.0003) is much smaller than typical run-to-run noise, so its variance may be underestimated. This is not a reason to veto.
Side note: the smaller model probably uses less VRAM and less time per step, so it is unlikely to run into the 450 s limit.
